children.html: A cart and pendulum, shown below, consists of a cart of mass, m_1, moving on a horizontal surface, acted upon by a spring with spring constant k. From the cart is suspended a pendulum consisting of a uniform rod of length, l, and mass, m_2, pivoting about point A.
Derive the equations of motion for this system by Lagrange. Specifically,
• Find T, the system's kinetic energy
• Find V, the system's potential energy
• Find v_G^2, the square of the magnitude of the pendulum's center of gravity
The linear velocity of the pendulum's center of mass, v_G, is given by
The square of its magnitude is given by

T = \frac{1}{2} m_{1} \dot{x}^{2} + \frac{1}{2} m_{2} v_{G}^{2} + \frac{1}{2} I_{G} \dot{\theta}^{2} T = \frac{1}{2} m_{1} \dot{x}^{2} + \frac{1}{2} m_{2} \bigl(\dot{x}^{2} + \dot{x}\dot{\theta}\,l\cos\theta + \frac{l^{2}\dot{\theta}^{2}}{4}\bigr) + \frac{1}{2} \bigl(\frac{m\,l^{2}}{12}\bigr) \dot{\theta}^{2}
V = \frac{1}{2} k x^{2} + \frac{m_{2} g l}{2} \bigl(1 - \cos\theta\bigr)

\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{2} m_{1} \dot{x}^{2} + \frac{1}{2} m_{2} \Bigl(\dot{x}^{2} + \dot{x}\,\dot{\theta}\,l\cos\theta + \frac{l^{2}\dot{\theta}^{2}}{4}\Bigr) + \frac{1}{2} \Bigl(\frac{m l^{2}}{12}\Bigr)\dot{\theta}^{2} - \frac{1}{2} k x^{2} - m_{2} g \frac{l}{2} \bigl(1 - \cos\theta\bigr)
Lagrange's equation for the first generalized coordinate,
yields the first equation of motion.
(m_1 + m_2)\ddot{x} + \frac{m_2 l}{2}\ddot{\theta}\cos\theta - \frac{m_2 l}{2}\dot{\theta}^2 \sin\theta + kx = 0 \tag{1}
Lagrange's equation for the second generalized coordinate,
yields the second equation of motion.
\left(\frac{m_2 l^2}{4} + \frac{m_2 l^2}{12}\right)\ddot{\theta} + \frac{m_2 l}{2}\ddot{x}\cos\theta + m_2 g \frac{l}{2}\sin\theta = 0\tag{2}
Assume that the cart and pendulum system now contain a damper/dashpot of constant b between the cart and ground, as well as an external force, F(t), applied to the cart.
Derive the equations of motion for this system by Lagrange. Specifically, show the generalized forces.
Both the damper and the external force are non-conservative (forces). Consequently, they enter the Lagrange formulation as generalized forces.

\delta W^{nc} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbf{f}_{i}^{nc} \cdot \delta \mathbf{R}_{i} = \sum_{j=1}^{n} Q_{j}\,\delta\xi_{j}
\delta W^{nc} = \bigl[-b\dot{x} + F(t)\bigr]\,\delta x + [0]\,\delta\theta
Q_{x} = -b\dot{x} + F(t) \qquad Q_{\theta} = 0

So our equations of motion become

(m_{1} + m_{2})\ddot{x} + \frac{m_{2}l}{2}\ddot{\theta}\cos\theta - \frac{m_{2}l}{2}\dot{\theta}^{2}\sin\theta + b\dot{x} + kx = F(t)

(3)
\Bigl(\frac{m_2 l^2}{4} + \frac{m_2 l^2}{12}\Bigr)\ddot{\theta} + \frac{m_2 l}{2}\ddot{x}\cos\theta + m_2 g \frac{l}{2}\sin\theta = 0 \tag{4}
